claim: Monte Carlo statistical companion to sim/pll-lock's PVT sweep (issue #20's second acceptance-criteria bullet): the closed-loop PLL (design/top/top.sch -- VCO + PFD/charge pump + loop filter + divider, issue #28), driven from the same cold start sim/pll-lock uses (RESETB power-on, the loop filter's three storage nodes explicitly initialized discharged), at one fixed PVT point (this manifest's `monte_carlo` block), resampled across a population of sky130 local-mismatch + die-to-die process draws, and reduced by sim/harness/measure.py's period-jitter extractor once locked. This is the Monte Carlo half of the verification DR-006 (spec/decision-records/DR-006-statistical-rows-ratification.md) states for ratified target-spec row 9 (period jitter, <= 1.0% of the output period RMS, at CLK in lock) -- 'verified over [the ratified PVT grid] plus a local-mismatch Monte Carlo population'. The PVT half is sim/pll-lock's own sweep; this experiment does not repeat that axis (see monte_carlo.corner/temp_c/supply_v below for the single point it samples at).
spec_rows_note: target-spec.md row 9 (period jitter), RATIFIED via DR-006 (#151/#160). This is this row's Monte Carlo evidence: a population of local-mismatch + process draws at one PVT point, reduced by measure.period_jitter() once a trial locks. Lock time (row 8, DRAFT) and duty cycle (row 14, DRAFT) are also reported per trial (the same reducer sim/pll-lock uses), but this experiment's citation is row 9 -- the reason it exists.

monte_carlo.claim: row 9's Monte Carlo population: local-mismatch (MC_MM_SWITCH) + die-to-die process (MC_PR_SWITCH) draws at tt/125C/1.80V. Every trial shares this fixed (corner, temperature, supply); only the RNG seed -- and therefore the sampled device draw -- varies. Both sampling switches are on, so the population is a superset of the 'local-mismatch Monte Carlo population' DR-006 names for row 9 (it also carries die-to-die process spread on top of the tt base corner) -- broader than the ratified minimum, never narrower. Base point chosen as the one point in this DUT's history with a *documented* cold-start lock under the same nudge/discharged-loop-filter convention this manifest inherits: design/top/DESIGN.md's issue-#98 probe 3 (tt/125C/1.80V, kicked, 30 us window) locks at 26.32 us, f_out 251.5 MHz. It is deliberately NOT ss/-40C/1.80V, the point sim/pll-lock/records/20260905-193322-0f1934d.md shows locking in 1.711 us: that record predates DR-005's discharged-loop-filter initial conditions, and the same #98 probe measured t=0 VCTRL at 0.900 V at exactly that point, so its fast lock rode an unphysical loop-filter pre-charge this manifest explicitly removes. A calibration run of this manifest at ss/-40C/1.80V with a 5 us window (--no-write, not evidence) observed zero output edges, confirming that the 1.711 us figure does not transfer.
monte_carlo.methodology_note: process_corners/temps_c/supply_tolerance above are declared for schema symmetry with every other tb.json in this repo, but this experiment has never been run in `sim/run_corners.py`'s plain PVT mode (no PVT record exists under sim/pll-lock-mc/records/) -- its whole claim is the `--mc` campaign this block configures. `require_lock: false` (measure block): a trial that completes but never locks is recorded as evidence (no lock within this window, at this draw), not as a harness failure -- consistent with sim/pll-lock's own convention -- and per measure.py's own rule contributes no jitter figure either, since row 9's population is post-lock. `measure.jitter.gate_on_bound: true` (also measure.py's own default once a `jitter` block names a `max_frac`): a locked trial whose jitter exceeds the ratified 1.0% bound, or that locks with fewer than the required 20 post-lock cycles, fails that trial -- a miss against a ratified row is recorded as a miss, per CLAUDE.md, never silently folded into a plumbing-only PASS. `tran_stop` (50 us) is sized as the 26.32 us documented cold-start lock time at this base point plus ~24 us of post-lock tail (~6000 output cycles at 250 MHz, far more than `jitter.min_cycles` = 20), not as sim/pll-lock's own 100 us row-8 lock-time budget window: this campaign's citation is row 9, a post-lock quantity, so it buys post-lock population rather than the full cold-start budget row 8 is stated over. The consequence is stated rather than hidden -- a draw that would have locked between 50 us and row 8's 100 us budget is recorded here as 'no lock within 50 us', which is a limitation of THIS window, not a row-8 verdict; sim/pll-lock's own 100 us grid is where that question belongs. Simulator accuracy (issue #202), stated because row 9's bound is tight against it and because the record this campaign's first re-run supersedes (20260924-222341-a9375a5) ran without it: `measure.options` injects `.options reltol=1e-4`, and the transient is `tran 20p 50u 0 200p` -- a 20 ps dump grid with ngspice's internal-step cap (TMAX) held at the 200 ps it always had. Both are measurement-accuracy settings, not a window change and not a spec change: the window, lock criterion, jitter population and ratified 1.0% bound are unchanged. The reason is measured, not argued -- sim/integrator-floor runs design/vco's ring open-loop at this campaign's own operating point (tt/125C/1.80V, ~250 MHz), where its true period jitter is zero by construction, and reports 1.543% RMS at the settings 20260924-222341-a9375a5 ran under (ngspice's default reltol=1e-3, 200 ps grid; record 20260925-201301-d8b1ab7), 0.658% with reltol=1e-4 alone (20260925-201647-d8b1ab7, the residual being sim/jitter-floor's dump-grid floor for this ring's ~74 ps edge), and 0.005% with both (20260925-203420-d8b1ab7). A campaign whose own null control reports more than the bound cannot distinguish a design that meets row 9 from one that misses it. Cost: the tighter reltol roughly triples-to-quadruples the number of internal timepoints; the finer grid costs nothing in integration (TMAX is unchanged, measured: the same 109,986 vs 109,989 internal steps over a 6 us open-loop run) and only enlarges the uncommitted dump. `timeout_s` is raised to 12 h for that reason.
monte_carlo.analysis: cold-start transient, closed loop, one sky130 statistical draw per trial (`tran 20p 50u 0 200p` under `.options reltol=1e-4`, injected by sim/harness/measure.py from this manifest's own measure block, exactly as sim/pll-lock's PVT points are -- see sim/harness/runner.py's patch_netlist_mc for how the MC_MM_SWITCH/MC_PR_SWITCH/seed cards and this control block combine ahead of the netlist's .end)

methodology_note: this testbench's DUT is design/top/top.sch, the real four-block closed-loop PLL (not a throwaway circuit) -- straps NSEL[5:0]=011000 (N=25) and drives REF with a 10 MHz clock and RESETB with a power-on reset pwl, identically to sim/pll-lock/testbench/tb_pll_lock.sch (this schematic is a verbatim copy of it, see tb_pll_lock_mc.sch's own header comment for why a distinct file exists per this repo's one-directory-per-distinct-claim convention). `measure.ic` forces the same cold-start nudge/discharged-loop-filter initial conditions sim/pll-lock's own manifest uses (see its methodology_note and spec/decision-records/DR-004/DR-005 for the evidentiary justification) -- this experiment does not re-argue that choice, it inherits it. See this manifest's own `monte_carlo.methodology_note` for the Monte-Carlo-specific choices (base point, window sizing, gating).
